newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo control of JSE slips to under 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Anglo control of JSE slips to under 25 pct.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's control by market capitalisation of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) has slipped to 24 percent from 60 percent 10 years ago, according to research published on Wednesday.
McGregor Information Services, publisher of Who Owns Whom, said the shift reflected the substantial fall in the price of gold as well as the hiving off of operations to new black business groups.
"The rise of black control is unprecedented even by that of the Afrikaners which began with their successful bid for control of General Mining in 1964," said director Simon McGregor.

In 1995 blacks controlled only 0.3 percent of JSE market capitalisation. Today, following the change of ownership at Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) and JCI Ltd, their share has risen to nine percent.
Foreigners now control 66 listed companies representing 4.7 percent of market capitalisation, up from 46 companies representing 1.9 percent in 1991.
